claims.claim: Haas dropped Ocon for the rest of the Mexico City weekend with no reason given
claims.note: RaceFans and F1 say no reason was given.

claims.claim: The team confirmed Ocon was not ill
claims.note: RaceFans quotes the team statement.

claims.claim: Hirakawa was called up on Saturday morning, before qualifying
claims.note: F1 says the change was announced on Saturday morning.

claims.claim: He was due to partner Ollie Bearman through final practice and qualifying
claims.note: F1 names Bearman as team mate for Saturday.

claims.claim: Sunday's 71-lap race was his first Grand Prix start
claims.note: F1 calls the 71-lap race his Formula 1 race debut.

claims.claim: He took part in Friday's opening practice as reserve driver
claims.note: RaceFans says he took part in the opening practice session.

claims.claim: He finished 15th overall in Friday practice
claims.note: F1 quotes 15th overall.

claims.claim: Ocon returned during the second practice session and was 13th, ahead of Bearman
claims.note: F1 says Ocon returned to action in the second hour; RaceFans gives 13th ahead of Bearman.

claims.claim: He qualified 19th and was eliminated in Q1
claims.note: F1 gives P19 and says missing Q1 was a shame for him.

claims.claim: He had traffic on his last push lap
claims.note: Quoted from F1.

claims.claim: He called the call-up a dream come true
claims.note: F1 quotes dream come true.

claims.claim: Official reserve driver for Haas from April 2025
claims.note: F1 article dated 7 April 2025 and Haas profile.

claims.claim: Moved from Alpine and will help with car development as well as reserve duties
claims.note: F1 says he had been part of Alpine's stable and will help with car development.

claims.claim: Haas profile lists four practice sessions with the team: Bahrain, Spain, Mexico City and Abu Dhabi
claims.note: Profile lists FP1 appearances at those venues.

claims.claim: Earlier practice running came with McLaren
claims.note: Profile lists McLaren official reserve driver 2024 and an FP1 appearance. F1 article does not mention McLaren.

claims.claim: At Alpine he was official test and reserve driver and ran one practice session at the Japanese Grand Prix in Suzuka
claims.note: Profile lists Alpine test and reserve role and an FP1 at the Japanese Grand Prix.

claims.claim: He drove for Haas in the post-season test in Abu Dhabi in December 2024
claims.note: F1 says he drove in the Abu Dhabi post-season test last December.

claims.claim: Ocon was due to leave Haas at the end of 2026; Rafael Camara replaces him
claims.note: RaceFans: Ocon due to leave at season's end, Ferrari junior Camara takes his place next year.

claims.claim: Born 7 March 1994 in Hiroshima, Japan
claims.note: Haas profile gives birth date and birthplace.

claims.claim: Won the All-Japan Junior Kart Championship in 2008
claims.note: Profile lists the title.

claims.claim: Runner-up in Formula Challenge Japan in 2011 and 2012
claims.note: Profile gives 2011 (73 points) and 2012 (91 points) runner-up.

claims.claim: Won the 2012 Japanese Formula 3 championship and the Porsche Carrera Cup Japan title
claims.note: Profile lists both titles in 2012.

claims.claim: Qualified 24th for the 2012 Macau Grand Prix and did not finish
claims.note: Profile gives qualifying 24th and a retirement.

claims.claim: Raced in Super Formula from 2013 to 2015 and from 2018 to 2023
claims.note: Profile lists these seasons.

claims.claim: Won the 2017 GT500 Super GT title with TOM'S and was runner-up in 2018, 2019 and 2020
claims.note: Profile lists the title and runner-up seasons.

claims.claim: European Le Mans Series: fifth in 2016 with Thiriet by TDS, fourth in 2017 with G-Drive Racing
claims.note: Profile gives 5th (2016) and 4th (2017).

claims.claim: Races for Toyota in the FIA World Endurance Championship
claims.note: F1 says he competes for Toyota GAZOO Racing in the WEC.

claims.claim: Won the 2022 24 Hours of Le Mans with the team
claims.note: Profile lists pole and victory at Le Mans 2022 with Toyota.

claims.claim: Formula 1 calls him a two-time WEC champion
claims.note: F1 says two-time champion, without years.

claims.claim: WEC titles in 2022 (149 points) and 2023 (172 points); fourth in 2024 (109) and seventh in 2025 (66)
claims.note: Profile gives all four seasons and points.

claims.claim: RaceFans reports he normally races for Toyota in the WEC and is due to return there
claims.note: RaceFans: scheduled to return to his regular Toyota seat.

claims.claim: Haas has not said whether Hirakawa will keep the seat for the rest of the season
claims.note: RaceFans says Haas did not indicate he will remain.

claims.claim: The team statement ended: No further statements will be made at this time.
claims.note: Quoted from F1.

claims.claim: Quote: a very big surprise this morning
claims.note: F1 quote: Obviously was a very big surprise this morning.

claims.claim: Quote: I was ready but always dreaming about it
claims.note: Quoted from F1.

claims.claim: Quote: Just these 12 hours passed so fast
claims.note: Quoted from F1.

claims.claim: Quote: Very excited for that.
claims.note: Quoted from F1.

valueNote: Sets out the Ocon call-up timeline with the session-by-session results and the Haas, Alpine and WEC record in one place, with sources for each.
summary: All checked claims match the fetched sources after the fixes to the partner, WEC-years and FP2 wording; the racer.com page returned 429 and is not cited.
